thread:
morgan: Quick brain dump — ran the sim on hybrid "burst-pool + steady" approach. results are promising but a few edge cases.

priya: drop numbers pls, curious about tail latency and eviction counts.

morgan: numbers: 99th latency down 18% vs strict-reservation, avg cost +2%. peak eviction rate went up 12% but most were <30s.

jon: 12% eviction increase worries me. Are those preemptions user-facing or internal retries?

morgan: mostly user requests getting killed (low-priority) to make room for steady reservations when load spikes. Not ideal.

emi: what about a small immutable safety headroom per shard to reduce visible preempts? e.g., keep 8% of pool as non-burstable slack.

morgan: we tried headroom=8% in sim, eviction delta drops to 3% and latency benefit persists (99th -12%). tradeoff is slightly higher cost.

priya: how do you track burst consumption? global bank or per-shard?
morgan: current sim used a local per-shard bucket that accrues per-tenant/token at rate r. bucket semantics: top-up continuously, cap at C, consume on admission.

jon: per-shard is simpler but invites cross-shard unfairness. any plan to reconcile?
morgan: proposal: per-shard initially + daily reconciliation job that redistributes unused tokens across shards for the same tenant. cheap and eventual consistent.

emi: curious about multi-slot requests: if a request needs 3 GPUs and only per-slot tokens exist, do we reserve across slots atomically?
morgan: admission is atomic at runtime: we try to lock k slots; if fail we roll back and optionally borrow burst tokens across slots in the same shard. We avoid partial starts.

priya: that implies two-phase: tentative reserve -> lock -> confirm charge. how long is tentative?
morgan: tentative TTL = 45s in sim. If the job doesn't confirm (container started) we refund. reduces wrongfully charged tokens on quick preempts.

jon: ops question: what about controller vs runtime mismatch? controllers might optimistically assume admission.

morgan: include admit metadata in runtime response: admit=true/false, admit_reason, burst_used, tentative=true/false, lease_expiry. controller stores that and reconciles.

emi: nice. add metric labels: tenant_id, shard_id, request_shape (gpus), priority, tentative_flag.

infra-bot: Canary deploy queued: feature/burst-pool-experiment -> canary (build #5110) :rocket:

priya: rollout plan? we should start with low-risk tenants and a short experiment window.
morgan: plan: 1) FF off. 2) enable for <10 tenants in canary for 72h. 3) collect metrics: evictions, tentative-refunds, headroom-util, 99/95/50 latencies, cost-per-token. 4) iterate and increase ramp.

jon: what about SLOs — if we leak headroom and see tail breaks we need auto-disable.
morgan: added auto-disable rule: if 99th latency increase >10% for more than 15m on any shard, FF flips off for that shard.

emi: testing: we need an integration harness that replays spike traces and also fuzzes scheduler races. Can we wire that into CI?
morgan: yes, small harness prototype exists. i'll PR next week with scripts and sim data.

priya: doc this as an RFC + checklist. Keep it incremental.
morgan: will do — i'll open RFC with schema, metrics, rollout steps, and operator kill-switch. thanks all.

jon: small ask — add a config snippet in RFC for operators.
morgan: snippet i'll include:```
pool: dedicated-prod-eu
burst_enabled: true
burst_accrual_per_min: 0.4
burst_cap: 10
shard_safety_headroom_pct: 8
tentative_ttl_secs: 45
auto_disable_latency_pct: 10
```

emi: looks solid. thanks for running sims.

infra-bot: Canary deploy started: feature/burst-pool-experiment -> canary (build #5110) :white_check_mark:

morgan: ping when canary metrics land, i'll start the RFC draft.
